issue_context.title: Attribute "expired" not considered for the status
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hello together!

I´m really thankful for this integration!
Just one thing is bugging me: The first sensor´s status is still "on", even though the NINA app isn´t showing warnings anymore.
So I guess that the attribute "expires" is not considered?

`headline: Amtliche WARNUNG vor STARKEM GEWITTER
description: >-
  Es treten Gewitter auf. Dabei gibt es Sturmböen mit Geschwindigkeiten um 70
  km/h (20m/s, 38kn, Bft 8) sowie Starkregen mit Niederschlagsmengen um 20 l/m²
  pro Stunde.
sender: Deutscher Wetterdienst
severity: Moderate
id: >-
  dwd.2.49.0.0.276.0.DWD.PVW.1659641580000.0cfd2285-8fbe-491d-bf8a-88c78af642dc.MUL
sent: '2022-08-04T21:32:37+02:00'
start: '2022-08-04T21:33:00+02:00'
expires: '2022-08-04T22:15:00+02:00'
device_class: safety
friendly_name: 'Warning: Brakel, Stadt (Höxter - Nordrhein-Westfalen) 1'`

Last refresh was 10 minutes after the expiration date.

Hey there @deermaximum, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`nina`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L721) for? Thanks!

review_comments:
Update the return value type annotation here and in `_async_update_data` and in the custom class definition of the generic coordinator. It should be:
```py
dict[str, list[NinaWarningData]]
```
We wouldn't need the explicit type annotation here with a correctly annotated coordinator above.
